headline: Daily market snapshot July 30 2026
summary: Composite of major index, yield, commodity, FX, and crypto levels as of the July 29-30 2026 window, sourced from multiple financial outlets.

headline: Fed holds rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% in divided 9-3 vote
summary: The Federal Reserve voted 9-3 to keep the benchmark rate unchanged at 3.5%-3.75% for the fifth consecutive meeting. Three regional Fed presidents—Hammack (Cleveland), Kashkari (Minneapolis), and Logan (Dallas)—dissented, citing persistent inflation above the 2% target for more than five years. Markets reacted negatively, with bond yields surging and stocks tumbling.
key_facts: Rate held at 3.5%-3.75% for fifth straight meeting
FOMC noted 'solid pace' of activity despite Middle East uncertainty
Markets pricing two 25bp rate hikes in 2026

headline: Bond yields at 19-year high as market rout follows Fed decision
summary: Following the Fed's hawkish hold, the 30-year Treasury yield surged as much as 14 basis points to near 5.23%, its highest level in nearly two decades. The 10-year yield rose to 4.66%. Investors dumped long-dated bonds, signaling fears the Fed is falling behind on inflation control, and Australian, New Zealand, and Japanese bonds followed.
key_facts: Global bonds followed; Australia, NZ, Japan yields rose
Bond market signaling Fed may be behind on inflation

headline: Meta Q2 2026: Revenue beats at $60.8B but EPS misses at $6.18 vs $7.10 estimate; stock -9.6% AH
summary: Meta reported Q2 2026 revenue of $60.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year and beating the $60.18 billion estimate, but EPS of $6.18 missed the $7.10 consensus by nearly $1. Total expenses surged 55% YoY to $42.0 billion, including a $2.4 billion legal contingency charge and $1.2 billion in severance costs. Shares fell 9.64% in after-hours trading to $529.15.

headline: Meta narrows 2026 capex guidance to $130B-$145B, fueling AI spending concerns
summary: Meta's raised capital expenditure range of $130B-$145B for 2026 renewed investor concerns about the ROI of AI infrastructure investment. The outsized AI spending alongside an EPS miss triggered a historic extended losing streak in the stock and broader AI-spending sentiment deteriorated.
key_facts: Investor concerns about AI spending ROI
Spending concerns spread to broader AI sector

headline: Microsoft Q2 CY2026: Revenue $90.01B beats, Azure +38%, EPS $4.81 vs $4.22 estimate
summary: Microsoft reported calendar Q2 2026 results with revenue of $90.01 billion, up 17.7% year-over-year and beating the $87.71 billion estimate. Non-GAAP EPS of $4.81 beat the $4.22 consensus. Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion annualized for the first time, growing 38% in constant currency. Commercial remaining performance obligation hit $625 billion, up 110% YoY.
key_facts: Azure revenue +38% constant currency, surpassed $100B first time

headline: Alphabet Q2 2026: Revenue $119.8B (+24%) but first-ever negative FCF of -$5.85B since 2004 IPO
summary: Alphabet reported Q2 2026 revenue of $119.8 billion, up 24% year-over-year, with Google Cloud surging 82% to $24.8 billion. However, capital expenditures of $44.9 billion exceeded operating cash flow of $39.1 billion, producing a negative free cash flow of -$5.85 billion—the first quarterly negative FCF since the company's 2004 IPO. Full-year capex guidance was raised to $195-205 billion.
key_facts: Free cash flow -$5.85B, first negative since 2004 IPO

The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $3.9B-$4.2B, representing approximately 100% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Shares advanced 11% to $185.85.

Management raised full-year organic revenue growth guidance and comparable EPS growth outlook to 9%-10%.

summary: Boeing reported Q2 2026 revenue of $24.6 billion, up 8% year-over-year and above the $24.26 billion consensus, as commercial jet deliveries rose to 171 from 150 a year ago. Revenue of $5.63 billion beat the $5.44 billion consensus and rose 6.8% year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA grew 16.3% to $1.304 billion. Management raised full-year guidance and authorized a $2 billion share buyback.

The selloff was driven by fears over Chinese chip competition from ChangXin Memory Technologies and concerns about the sustainability of AI capital spending.
